senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to bore holes, to carry thread through a hole,]

units: <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:10">Cant. R. to I, 10</cite> (ref. to <he>בחרוזים</he> <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:10">ib.</cite>) <he>שחוֹרְזִים צואריהם וכ׳</he> (not <he>שחוזרין</he>) who squeeze their necks (through window holes, open doors &c.) to hear the words of the Law (v.

<cite ref="Yoma 35b">Yoma 35ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Berakhot 6b">Ber. 6ᵇ</cite>; v. <cite ref="D00231"><he>דּוּחֲקָא</he></cite>); Yalk. ib. 983 <he>שהם חוזרים אחרי וכ׳</he> (read: <he>חוֹרְזִים אחוֹרֵי</he>).

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 20:9">Ex. R. s. 20</cite> <he>ישב וח׳ וכ׳</he> he sat down and strung (assorting) the larger pearls separately &c.—Part. pass. <cite ref="H01621"><he>חָרוּז</he></cite>, pl. <he>חֲרוּזִים</he>, <he>חֲרוּזִין</he>. Cant. R. l. c. [read:] <he>אלו ע׳ זקנים שהיו חֲרוּזִים אחריהם כליניא וכ׳</he> (v. Yalk. l. c.) those are the seventy elders who were strung (arranged) behind them (Moses and Aaron) like a string of pearls.—
<cite ref="Chullin 95b:15">Ḥull. 95ᵇ</cite> <he>בחרוזין</he> (Ar. <he>חֲרִיזִים</he>, noun) if the pieces of meat are strung together.

Lam. R. to V, 13 ג׳ מאות … ח׳ וכ׳ three hundred children were found strung up on the branches of one tree.—Trnsf. to draw parallels between Biblical passages, to explain one passage by another. Cant. R. l. c. הייתי יושב וחוֹרֵז וכ׳ I was sitting and comparing verses of the Pentateuch, and Pentateuch with Prophets &c.—Ib. שהיו חוֹרְזִים וכ׳; Yalk. l. c. חוזרים (corr. acc.). Cant. R. l. c. שהן חֲרוּזוֹת וכ׳ which are strung together (illustrate one another).
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 16">Lev. R. s. 16</cite> <he>מַחֲרִיז ד״ת וכ׳</he> I was comparing &c.
